title: Implement APVTS layout processBlock and latency
description:
Rewrite Source/PluginProcessor.cpp only (depends on e.1 header). Single owner for this file in phase e.

Implement:
1) createParameterLayout() with all 19 parameters exactly as specified by the project parameter table/IDs:
   MAX_ENABLE, MAX_PROCESS, MAX_CONTOUR, MAX_LOW_FREQ, MAX_HIGH_FREQ, MAX_PHASE_MODE,
   EXC_ENABLE, EXC_TUNE, EXC_DRIVE, EXC_MIX, EXC_MODE, EXC_HARMONICS, EXC_AIR_GAIN,
   ROUTING_MODE, PARALLEL_BLEND, MASTER_IN_GAIN, MASTER_OUT_GAIN, MASTER_MIX, OVERSAMPLING
   — ranges, defaults, skews, and choice options must match the specification table exactly so later editor attachments do not break.
2) Constructor/destructor: construct APVTS with createParameterLayout(); own DSP instances; init AbstractFifo/spectrum buffer; cache atomic/SmoothedValue parameter pointers.
3) prepareToPlay: pre-allocate all DSP/oversampling/buffers; no allocations later on the audio thread; reset smoothers; compute and call setLatencySamples() from the selected oversampling factor.
4) processBlock: first statement must be juce::ScopedNoDenormals; then master input gain -> RoutingEngine (SonicMaximizer / AuralExciter path per routing) -> master output gain and dry/wet (MASTER_MIX); read parameters via atomics/SmoothedValue only (no locks, no heap, no freestore on the audio thread); push spectrum frames into the SPSC FIFO for UI.
5) releaseResources / reset as needed for owned DSP.
6) createEditor: keep returning the generic/existing editor path for now — do NOT wire the real split-screen PluginEditor (later phase).
7) Latency: whenever oversampling changes or in prepareToPlay, report latency via setLatencySamples() tracking the oversampling factor.

Real-time safety is mandatory on the audio path.

Before editing, inspect:
- Source/PluginProcessor.h (from e.1)
- Source/PluginProcessor.cpp (phase-a stub)
- SonicMaximizer / AuralExciter / RoutingEngine headers and APIs
- parameter specification table (19 IDs/ranges/defaults/skews)
- JUCE APVTS patterns already used in the tree if any

STRICT FILE SCOPE: Create or modify ONLY the files listed in this task's allowed_write_paths.
